origin.summary: Every weight of the official Qwen3-0.6B-Base (Apache-2.0) was fine-tuned (nothing frozen, no adapter) together with a new candidate head trained from random initialization, and the release is the uniform average of three seeds of that fine-tune. It contains no Decision 1.0 Kai or Lex weights: Decision 1.0 Kai is the comparison model, and our own Decision 1.0 Lux-9B supplied soft training targets only.

runtime_requirements.torch: 2.12.0+git6bbd260 (ROCm 7.2 build; one ROCm GPU and CPU tested)

runtime_equivalence: decision2/qwen.py loads this full checkpoint with the vendored training/model sources whose SHA-256 equal the scored adapter sources (checked at build time) and applies the per-state batching (all questions of one state in one batch), BF16-backbone / FP32-head execution, the CAL698 per-type temperatures in calibration.json and the answer normalization of training.model.infer (adapter decision2-typed with --calibration). The calibrated predictions are the scored logits divided by the temperatures: answers are identical to the uncalibrated run on every scored prompt. Checked on one GPU of the scoring node against the sealed calibrated predictions by release.sh --parity.

scored.label: post-key same-panel run m4-t-a7-soup with CAL698 temperatures (frozen runner re-score, 8,192 tokens)

components.component: DEV2.0-0.6B weights, decision head, package runtime, card and artwork
Qwen3-0.6B-Base weights and tokenizer (direct weight origin, fully fine-tuned)

attributions: [Qwen3-0.6B-Base](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base) at `da87bfb608c14b7cf20ba1ce41287e8de496c0cd`: direct weight origin; every weight was fine-tuned (Apache-2.0, `LICENSES/Qwen3-0.6B-Base-LICENSE.txt`). The tokenizer files are the Qwen3 tokenizer as saved by the training code.

[Decision 1.0 Lux-9B](https://huggingface.co/llm-semantic-router/Decision-1.0-Lux-9B) (Apache-2.0), our own model: its probabilities on 6,430 training prompts were soft training targets. None of its weights are included.

Training data (not redistributed here; each keeps its own licence): GoEmotions (Demszky et al., ACL 2020; CC BY 4.0), SNLI (Bowman et al., EMNLP 2015; CC BY-SA 4.0), MultiNLI non-fiction genres (Williams, Nangia and Bowman, NAACL 2018; OANC terms), CLINC150 (Larson et al., EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019; CC BY 3.0), BANKING77 (Casanueva et al., 2020; CC BY 4.0), KLUE STS (Park et al., 2021; CC BY-SA 4.0), JGLUE JSTS (Kurihara et al., LREC 2022; CC BY-SA 4.0), IBM ArgQ-30k (Gretz et al., AAAI 2020; CC BY-SA 3.0), SAF (Filighera et al., ACL 2022; CC BY 4.0), and project-generated decision tasks.

Evaluation data shown on the card: JevArena v3 and JevBench public 231 (panels described in `evaluation/EVALUATION.md`); mlx-diag Choice from the MASSIVE 1.1 test split (FitzGerald et al., 2022; CC BY 4.0) and Noul from the PAWS-X test split (Yang et al., EMNLP 2019).

Owl banner: Decision 1.0 Kai mosaic owl, unchanged pixels, in the DEV2.0 name layout; wordmark set in Poppins (SIL Open Font License) and DejaVu Sans Bold. The owl marks the 0.6B size tier; the model weights do not derive from Kai.

card.calibration_text: per-type temperatures fitted for this exact checkpoint on the clean 698-item calibration partition at the 8,192-token limit (Choice 0.592, Noul 0.588, Score 0.345; `calibration.json`). They sharpen the probabilities and leave every answer and accuracy unchanged; the score table reports typed Brier and 10-bin ECE of the calibrated probabilities.
card.requirements_text: Tested with Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.12 and Transformers 5.17 on one ROCm GPU (BF16 backbone, FP32 head), where answers match the evaluated predictions, and on CPU (FP32), where probabilities can differ from the GPU results by a few thousandths. Transformers 5.17 prints a Mistral tokenizer-regex warning when it finds the package's root `config.json`; it does not change tokenization and can be ignored.

text.tagline: A compact decision model for routing choices, yes/no checks and rubric scores over one state: native System One Choice, Noul and Score answers with probabilities, no chat API.
text.architecture: The 28-layer Qwen3-0.6B text backbone (causal attention) reads the state, the question and every supplied candidate once; a shared candidate head scores the candidates against a global query and returns probabilities without generating text.

text.comparator_note: GLiNER2.5-Decide declares Apache-2.0 in its model card metadata, but its repository has no LICENSE file.
details: **Weights:** the uniform average of three full fine-tunes of Qwen3-0.6B-Base with the same recipe, start and head initialization; the seeds differ only in data order, and each seed's checkpoint was chosen on a held-out selection set (all three at update 1,433 of 1,638).
training: **Recipe:** one epoch of full fine-tuning (1,638 updates of 16 rows; backbone learning rate 1e-5 with 10% warm-up and cosine decay, head 2e-4) with cross-entropy plus 0.5 × Brier, and a KL term (weight 1.0) toward soft targets from our own [Decision 1.0 Lux-9B](https://huggingface.co/llm-semantic-router/Decision-1.0-Lux-9B) on the 6,430 rows whose exact input it had labeled. No other teacher, and no outputs of Jev or of any third-party decision model.
**Data:** 26,203 decision rows (20.0M tokens): Choice 13,422, Noul 5,565 and Score 7,216 (2 to 10 levels); English 17,498, Chinese 6,722, Japanese 860, Korean 853 and German 270.

**Program-generated tasks (14,912 rows):** Decision 1.0 stage 1–4 generators and Decision 2.0 verifiable rule, counterfactual and multi-level Score generators, labeled by program oracles (no third-party text).

**Human labels (11,291 rows):** GoEmotions (CC BY 4.0), SNLI (CC BY-SA 4.0), MultiNLI non-fiction genres (OANC terms), CLINC150 (CC BY 3.0), BANKING77 (CC BY 4.0), KLUE STS and JGLUE JSTS (CC BY-SA 4.0), IBM ArgQ-30k (CC BY-SA 3.0) and SAF (CC BY 4.0).

**Not used:** two shortcut-prone reading families (Cosmos QA, SQuAD 2.0 answerability). Option keys that revealed the answer through their construction order were renumbered by position, and the training data were screened for overlap with the evaluation panels. Datasets keep their own licences ([attributions](ATTRIBUTIONS.md)).
limitations: **Typed Choice is below Decision 1.0 Kai:** 255 versus 277 of 800 JevArena v3 typed Choice questions (−22). The overall gain comes from Noul (442 vs 404), Score (133 vs 98) and human transfer (H 0.480 vs 0.357); the tradeoffs table lists every result below Kai.

**Same-limit comparison:** the table shows Decision 1.0 Kai at its published 1,024-token input limit. Run at this model's 8,192-token limit, Kai scores 35.97 on JevArena v3 and 127/231 on JevBench public, and the paired v3 difference is +7.57 (95% interval [+4.43, +10.59]).

**Not clearly ahead of the strongest 0.6B peer:** against GLiNER2.5-Decide the v3 difference is +1.02 with a paired 95% interval of [−1.77, +7.80], which includes zero; its typed accuracy T is higher (0.410 vs 0.395).

**Seed dependence:** the three single fine-tunes differed markedly on our development panels. Only their uniform average was evaluated and is released, so retraining the same recipe with another seed can give a noticeably weaker model.

**Calibration away from the calibration data:** the temperatures improve calibration on the in-distribution calibration partition (ECE 0.079 to 0.031) but worsen it on the evaluation panels: JevArena v3 typed ECE 0.191 versus 0.118 for the raw probabilities (Brier 0.332 vs 0.309), human-transfer median task ECE 0.120 vs 0.070. Treat probabilities as rankings more than as frequencies on unfamiliar inputs.

**Multilingual yes/no checks:** on the mlx-diag diagnostic, non-English Choice (intent routing) is 70.2%, but non-English Noul (paraphrase detection) is 51.8%, below Bosun v3.1 0.6B (61.2%); treat non-English Noul answers with care.
